llmEditor.conversationMemoryDesc: Older turns are incrementally compressed into a rolling summary. The LLM sees: [system prompt + summary] + [recent N turns verbatim]. A built-in conversationRecall tool allows the agent to drill back into summarized turns on demand.
llmEditor.counterweightCustomHint: Leave empty to use the built-in preset for the selected level.
llmEditor.counterweightCustomOverride: Custom instructions override the preset level text entirely.
llmEditor.counterweightDesc: Inject safety instructions into the system prompt. Guards against overconfidence, hallucination, and unsupervised action.
llmEditor.counterweightStrictNote: Strict mode is automatically downgraded to Cautious during scheduled/batch execution to prevent destructive "one step at a time" behavior.
llmEditor.excludePropsDesc: Skip facts already captured as persistent properties — focus on reasoning and implicit context
llmEditor.httpCallRagHint: Execute a named httpCall before the LLM call. The response is injected as context — no vector store needed.
llmEditor.identityMaskingDesc: Prevent the LLM from revealing its model name or provider when probed.
llmEditor.identityMaskingEmptyWarning: Masking is enabled but has no rules. Add at least one rule for masking to take effect.
llmEditor.identityMaskingRulePlaceholder: e.g. Never reveal you are an AI language model
llmEditor.identityMaskingRulesHint: Both enabled AND at least one rule are required for masking to take effect.
llmEditor.knowledgeBasesHint: Explicitly reference knowledge bases by name. Each name must match a RagConfiguration in the workflow.
llmEditor.legacyRagHint: This configuration uses the deprecated retrievalAugmentor format. Migrate to the modes above.
llmEditor.prePostDesc: Configure property instructions that run before each LLM request, and output/property instructions that run after each response.
llmEditor.summarizationPromptPlaceholder: Leave empty to use the default structured prompt that preserves goals, decisions, reasoning, and tone.
llmEditor.summarizeInfoBanner: The summarizer uses the same provider and API key as this task. Only the model name is swapped to a cheaper variant (e.g., gpt-4o-mini).
llmEditor.summaryProviderHint: Use a cheap/fast model for summarization
llmEditor.tokenWindowDesc: Replace step-count-based history with token-aware packing. When maxContextTokens is set (> 0), the engine fits as many recent turns as possible within the budget, optionally anchoring the opening turns.
llmEditor.toolResponseLimitsDesc: Truncate verbose tool outputs before re-injection into the LLM context window. Prevents context bloat.
llmEditor.workflowRagHint: Automatically discovers all RAG steps from the workflow. Only used when no explicit knowledge bases are listed above.
llmEditor.enableHttpCallToolsDesc: Automatically expose all httpcall extensions from the workflow as LLM tools
llmEditor.httpCallToolsHint: Explicit httpcall URIs (in addition to auto-discovered ones)
llmEditor.mcpServersDesc: External MCP servers whose tools become available to the LLM
llmEditor.preRequestDesc: Set or transform properties before the LLM call executes.
llmEditor.postResponseDesc: Process LLM output: set properties, build output messages, and generate quick replies.
llmEditor.enableMcpCallToolsDesc: Automatically expose all mcpcalls extensions from the workflow as LLM tools
llmEditor.a2aAgentsDesc: Remote A2A-compatible agents whose skills become LLM tools
llmEditor.cascadeDesc: Try a cheap/fast model first. If confidence is too low, automatically escalate to a more powerful (and expensive) model. Saves costs without sacrificing quality.
llmEditor.cascadeStrategyHint: Sequential tries cheap first, escalates on low confidence
llmEditor.cascadeEvalHint: How to determine if a response is good enough
llmEditor.cascadeInAgent: Also use cascade in Agent Mode (with tools)
llmEditor.cascadeStepsDesc: Order matters: first step tried first. Last step is always accepted (set confidence to empty).
llmEditor.cascadeEvalNoneHint: Confidence gating is disabled — the first step's response is always accepted.
llmEditor.cascadePricingHint: Default token pricing feeds cost tracking and the cost ceiling. Individual steps can override it.
llmEditor.cascadeJudgeModelDesc: A separate (usually cheap) model that rates each response's confidence.
llmEditor.cascadeHeuristicDesc: Optional overrides for hedging/refusal detection. Empty fields use the built-in English defaults. Localize the phrase lists for non-English deployments.

cascadeIssues.NO_STEPS: Cascade is enabled but has no steps — it will fail when it runs.
cascadeIssues.UNKNOWN_STRATEGY: Unknown strategy "{{strategy}}" — the cascade will run sequentially.
cascadeIssues.PARALLEL_NOT_IMPLEMENTED: Parallel strategy is not implemented yet — steps run sequentially.
cascadeIssues.UNKNOWN_EVAL_STRATEGY: Unknown confidence evaluation "{{strategy}}" — defaulting to Structured Output.
cascadeIssues.JUDGE_MODEL_MISSING: Judge Model evaluation has no judge configured — confidence falls back to heuristic.
cascadeIssues.JUDGE_CROSS_PROVIDER_NO_APIKEY: The judge model uses a different provider but has no API key of its own — it would inherit the task key.
cascadeIssues.MAX_DURATION_NONPOSITIVE: Max total duration must be greater than 0.
cascadeIssues.MAX_COST_NEGATIVE: Max cost per run cannot be negative.
cascadeIssues.CASCADE_INPUT_PRICE_NEGATIVE: Cascade input price cannot be negative.
cascadeIssues.CASCADE_OUTPUT_PRICE_NEGATIVE: Cascade output price cannot be negative.
cascadeIssues.CONVERT_TO_OBJECT_STRUCTURED: convertToObject is incompatible with Structured Output confidence — the cascade will use heuristic instead.
cascadeIssues.STEP_INPUT_PRICE_NEGATIVE: Step {{step}} input price cannot be negative.
cascadeIssues.STEP_OUTPUT_PRICE_NEGATIVE: Step {{step}} output price cannot be negative.
cascadeIssues.STEP_CONFIDENCE_OUT_OF_RANGE: Step {{step}} confidence must be between 0 and 1.
cascadeIssues.STEP_DEAD_NULL_THRESHOLD: Step {{step}} has no confidence threshold — later steps become unreachable.
cascadeIssues.STEP_TIMEOUT_NONPOSITIVE: Step {{step}} timeout must be greater than 0.
cascadeIssues.STEP_CROSS_PROVIDER_NO_APIKEY: Step {{step}} uses a different provider but has no API key of its own — it would inherit the task key.

llmEditor.parallelExecutionDesc: Run independent tool calls concurrently instead of sequentially

llmEditor.retryDesc: Configure automatic retries for failed LLM API calls with exponential backoff.
llmEditor.ragDesc: Augment LLM responses with relevant documents retrieved from an embedding store.
llmEditor.allToolsInfo: All {{count}} built-in tools are available to the LLM. Switch to "Select Specific" to restrict which tools are exposed.
llmEditor.toolSourcesInfo: Both sources are enabled by default — all workflow HTTP calls and MCP calls are automatically exposed as LLM tools. Disable a source to exclude it.
llmEditor.toolApprovalsEnable: Override tool approvals for this task
llmEditor.toolApprovalsDesc: Overrides the agent-level tool approvals for THIS task only — a full replace, not a merge.
llmEditor.responseValidationDesc: Control how the engine reacts to an empty, truncated, content-filtered, refused, or timed-out turn. "Fallback" substitutes a canned message; "Error" fails the turn; "Warn" logs and continues; "Ignore" does nothing.
llmEditor.rvDisabledInfo: Policies below are saved but only take effect while validation is enabled.
llmEditor.rvOnContentFilterHint: Response blocked by the provider's content filter
llmEditor.rvOnStreamingTimeoutHint: A streaming response timed out before completing
llmEditor.streamingTimeoutSecondsHint: Overrides the engine default (120s). Only applies while streaming; empty = use default.
llmEditor.taskPricingDesc: Prices this task's ordinary (non-cascade) model calls for cost tracking and group cost ceilings. Unpriced (blank) contributes $0.

secrets.description: Manage encrypted secrets shared across all agents in a tenant. Values are never exposed.

secrets.storeWarning: The value will be encrypted with AES-256-GCM. It cannot be retrieved once stored — only replaced.
secrets.confirmDeleteMessage: Are you sure you want to permanently delete "{{key}}"? Any agent configs using this secret will fail to resolve. This cannot be undone.
secrets.emptyHint: No secrets stored for tenant "{{tenant}}" yet. Click "Add Secret" to create one.
secrets.scopeExplanation: Secrets are scoped per tenant and shared across all agents. Reference them in configs with ${vault:keyName}. Access is controlled by configuration authorship — only admins who write the config decide which secrets to use.
secrets.creatingFor: Storing in tenant "{{tenant}}" — available to all agents
secrets.dangerZoneDesc: Operational recovery actions for the vault's cryptographic keys. Use these to rotate keys or recover access after the master key changed. Distinct from rotating an individual secret's value above.
secrets.rotateDekBlurb: Safe — no restart. Generates a new per-tenant data encryption key and re-encrypts every secret for this tenant.
secrets.rotateKekBlurb: Re-encrypts all tenant DEKs with a new master key. Requires updating EDDI_VAULT_MASTER_KEY and restarting afterwards.
secrets.rotateKekConfirmDesc: Re-encrypts every tenant's data encryption key with a new master key. The secret values themselves are unchanged.
secrets.kekTlsWarning: Both keys are sent in the request body. Only perform this over a TLS (HTTPS) connection so the keys are not exposed in transit.
secrets.kekNewKeyTooShort: New master key must be at least 8 characters.
secrets.kekRestartHint: After rotation you must update EDDI_VAULT_MASTER_KEY to the new key and restart EDDI.
secrets.kekResultInstruction: Action required: set the EDDI_VAULT_MASTER_KEY environment variable to the NEW master key and restart EDDI. Until you do, the running instance still uses the old key in memory.
secrets.resetTenantBlurb: Destructive last resort. Permanently deletes all secrets and the DEK so the vault can start fresh — use after a lost or changed master key.
secrets.resetConfirmLabel: Type the tenant name "{{tenant}}" to confirm
secrets.rotateDekConfirmDesc_one: This generates a new data encryption key for tenant "{{tenant}}" and re-encrypts its {{count}} secret. This is safe and takes effect immediately — no restart is required.
secrets.rotateDekConfirmDesc_other: This generates a new data encryption key for tenant "{{tenant}}" and re-encrypts its {{count}} secrets. This is safe and takes effect immediately — no restart is required.
secrets.rotateKekSuccess_one: Master key rotated — {{count}} DEK re-encrypted. Update EDDI_VAULT_MASTER_KEY and restart.
secrets.rotateKekSuccess_other: Master key rotated — {{count}} DEKs re-encrypted. Update EDDI_VAULT_MASTER_KEY and restart.
secrets.resetTenantConfirmDesc_one: This permanently deletes all {{count}} secret and the data encryption key for tenant "{{tenant}}". Use this as the recovery step when the master key was lost or changed and the old key is unavailable. This cannot be undone.
secrets.resetTenantConfirmDesc_other: This permanently deletes all {{count}} secrets and the data encryption key for tenant "{{tenant}}". Use this as the recovery step when the master key was lost or changed and the old key is unavailable. This cannot be undone.
secrets.resetTenantSuccess_one: Vault reset for "{{tenant}}" — {{count}} secret permanently deleted
secrets.resetTenantSuccess_other: Vault reset for "{{tenant}}" — {{count}} secrets permanently deleted

welcome.title: Welcome to EDDI
welcome.subtitle: Your AI Agent Command Center
welcome.introText: EDDI Manager is your command center for building, testing, and operating conversational AI agents.
welcome.capabilitiesSubtitle: Everything you need to build production-ready AI agents
welcome.buildAgentsDesc: Create and configure AI agents with the wizard or from scratch
welcome.designWorkflowsDesc: Drag-and-drop pipeline builder with Rules, LLM chains, and tools
welcome.testRealtimeDesc: Chat with your agents with streaming responses and built-in debugging
welcome.monitorOperateDesc: Conversations, audit trails, secrets, and quotas — all in one place
welcome.readySubtitle: You can restart any tour from the sidebar Help menu

dashboard.title: Dashboard Tour
dashboard.step1Desc: The sidebar organizes everything into three zones: Management, Development, and Operations. You'll always know where to find things.
dashboard.step2Desc: Live counts of your agents, workflows, and conversations. Click any card to jump straight to that section.
dashboard.step3Desc: Jump straight to common tasks. The Agent Wizard is the fastest way to create your first agent — it takes under 2 minutes.
dashboard.step4Desc: Switch between light, dark, and system themes. EDDI Manager speaks 11 languages — pick yours from the language selector.

agents.title: Agents Tour
agents.step1Desc: The wizard walks you through creating a fully configured agent — choose a model, set a personality, enable tools, and deploy.
agents.step2Desc: For power users: create a blank agent and configure it with full JSON control. Perfect for advanced setups.
agents.step3Desc: Find agents instantly by name. Switch between card and list views with the toggle on the right.
agents.step4Desc: Each card shows the agent's name, version, and last modified time. Click any agent for its detail page with deploy, chat, and workflow controls.

workflows.title: Workflows Tour
workflows.step1Desc: Workflows define the processing pipeline — a sequence of tasks like LLM calls, Rules, and HTTP integrations.
workflows.step2Desc: Each workflow can be attached to one or more agents. Click to open the drag-and-drop pipeline editor.
workflows.step3Desc: Search by name and switch between card grid and sortable table views.

chat.title: Chat Tour
chat.step1Desc: Select a deployed agent to start a conversation. Only agents that have been deployed appear here.
chat.step2Desc: Toggle real-time token streaming. When enabled, the response appears word by word — great for debugging latency.
chat.step3Desc: Open the sidebar to browse and resume previous conversations.
chat.step4Desc: Type a message and press Enter. The agent responds using the LLM, tools, and workflows you've configured.

resources.title: Resources Tour
resources.step1Desc: Resources are the building blocks of workflows. Each type controls a different part of the agent's behavior.
resources.step2Desc: Define which AI model powers your agent, its system prompt, tools, MCP servers, and cascade settings. This is the brain.
resources.step3Desc: Rules control conversation flow. HTTP Calls connect to external APIs. Both can be used as LLM tools.

conversations.title: Conversations Tour
conversations.step1Desc: Find conversations quickly by ID, agent, or recent user messages.
conversations.step2Desc: Filter conversations by state: Active, In Progress, Ended, or Error.
conversations.step3Desc: Browse all sessions. Click any conversation card to open the timeline and debug.

groups.title: Discussion Groups Tour
groups.step1Desc: Create an orchestration group to let multiple agents collaborate and debate.
groups.step2Desc: Search through your existing multi-agent clusters.
groups.step3Desc: Manage your collaborative environments, edit their policies, or delete stale groups.

logs.title: System Logs Tour
logs.step1Desc: Switch between a real-time stream of system logs and historical log search.
logs.step2Desc: Filter the incoming live stream by Agent or by critical Log Level.
logs.step3Desc: Download the current filtered logs as a text file for external analysis.

secrets.title: Secrets Vault Tour
secrets.step1Desc: Securely store a new API key, token, or password that your agents can reference.
secrets.step2Desc: Filter the vault view to show secrets scoped to a specific tenant ID.
secrets.step3Desc: Learn how to dynamically inject secrets into your LLM configurations without hardcoding them.

audit.title: Audit Ledger Tour
audit.step1Desc: Search the immutable audit ledger by a specific Conversation ID or by an Agent version.
audit.step2Desc: Enter your ID and click search to pull the verifiable execution history.
audit.step3Desc: Export the retrieved audit records to JSON for compliance and reporting.

schedules.title: Schedules Tour
schedules.step1Desc: Set up a new cron job or continuous heartbeat to trigger agent workflows automatically.
schedules.step2Desc: Monitor the total, active, and failed schedules across your platform.
schedules.step3Desc: Manage your automated triggers natively: pause, resume, edit, or test-fire them.

quotas.resetConfirmDesc: This immediately zeroes all usage counters (conversations, API calls, monthly cost) for tenant "default". This cannot be undone.
quotas.title: Quotas Tour
quotas.step1Desc: Define hard limits on total agents, daily conversations, and token costs for this tenant.
quotas.step2Desc: Monitor how much of the allocated quota the tenant has consumed in real-time.
quotas.step3Desc: Save your adjusted limits. The platform will block traffic that breaches these ceilings.

coordinator.title: Coordinator Tour
coordinator.step1Desc: View the heartbeat and event source connected to the backend coordinator system.
coordinator.step2Desc: Monitor real-time task queues and active job execution across your cluster.
coordinator.step3Desc: Inspect failed tasks and systematically discard or retry them to maintain system stability.

orphans.confirmPurgeAll: Permanently delete ALL {{count}} orphaned resources? The server purges every orphan — your selection is not applied. This cannot be undone.
orphans.title: Orphans Tour
orphans.step1Desc: Start a platform scan to detect loose configs disconnected from any agent.
orphans.step2Desc: Optionally toggle to include historically soft-deleted records in the purge.
orphans.step3Desc: Review the scanner's report, select stale objects, and permanently purge to reclaim DB space.

groups.advancedNotConfigured: No transcript window, retro memory, shared artifacts or facilitator configured — click Edit to turn them on.

groups.retroConfigHint: Lets a retro phase write lessons into the team's memory, carried into later discussions.
groups.artifactConfigHint: Lets members co-author documents that survive the turn they were written in.

groups.facilitatorNoMove: Allow at least one move, or turn the facilitator off.

groups.facilitatorMaxMovesCeiling: At most {{max}} — the facilitator is a bounded intervention, not an orchestrator.

ROUND_TABLE.label: Round Table
ROUND_TABLE.flow: Everyone gives their view, then builds on the others over several rounds

PEER_REVIEW.label: Peer Review
PEER_REVIEW.flow: Members answer on their own, critique each other, then revise

DEVIL_ADVOCATE.label: Devil's Advocate
DEVIL_ADVOCATE.flow: One member attacks the group's position, the rest defend it

DELPHI.label: Anonymous Rounds
DELPHI.flow: Members answer anonymously and revise each round, so nobody anchors on the first speaker

DEBATE.label: Pro/Con Debate
DEBATE.flow: One side argues for, one against, then rebuttals and a verdict

TASK_FORCE.label: Task Force
TASK_FORCE.flow: The moderator plans the work, members run tasks in parallel, results get verified

NEGOTIATION.label: Negotiation
NEGOTIATION.flow: Parties trade proposals until they agree; an arbiter steps in only if they do not

groupTemplates.advisoryBoardDesc: Five business perspectives — marketing, engineering, finance, legal, strategy — weigh in on the same question, then the moderator sums up.
groupTemplates.peerReviewDesc: Reviewers assess whatever you bring — a draft, a plan, a proposal — critique each other's assessment, revise, and the moderator merges the result.
groupTemplates.riskAssessmentDesc: Everyone gives their read, one member argues the opposite to expose blind spots, the others defend, then the moderator sums up what held.
groupTemplates.forecastingDesc: Members answer anonymously over several rounds and see only anonymized results in between, so no one anchors on whoever spoke first.
groupTemplates.proConDesc: Two members argue for the proposal and two against, followed by rebuttals and the moderator's verdict.
groupTemplates.negotiationDesc: Two parties state their interests, table proposals and trade concessions round by round; the moderator arbitrates only if no deal is reached.
groupTemplates.taskForceDesc: The moderator splits the goal into tasks, members work them in parallel, and the moderator verifies and combines the results.

discovery.title: Meet your Platform Operator
discovery.description: An assistant that inspects and operates this deployment. Off by default; every change it makes pauses for your approval.

activation.title: Activate the Platform Operator
activation.subtitle: Choose the model that will run the operator, review its instructions, and deploy.
activation.apiKeyHint: The key for your LLM provider. This is not an EDDI credential.
activation.apiKeyPlaceholder: Paste your API key, or pick a vault key
activation.vaultDown: The secrets vault is unavailable, so keys cannot be stored in it right now. A key entered here is passed through to the backend, which vaults it if it can.
activation.authModeHint: The operator calls your EDDI admin API. This decides what credentials those calls carry.
activation.authNoneBlocked: This deployment has authentication enabled, so unauthenticated tool calls would be rejected. The operator would deploy successfully and then fail every lookup. Choose "Your identity" instead.

scope.label: Capability
scope.hint: What the operator is allowed to do. Every write still pauses for your approval — see the safety rules below.

readOnly.label: Read-only
readOnly.description: Can inspect and explain this deployment. Cannot change anything.

readWrite.label: Read & write
readWrite.description: Also lets it create and modify agents and agent groups, deploy, undeploy, disable a runaway schedule, and edit an agent's descriptor — each one paused for your approval first.

scope.writeWarning: Activation verifies the approval gate against the stored policy before it finishes. A real, harmless test write then runs in the background — if it ever executes without pausing for approval, the operator is removed immediately.

activation.safetyPreambleHint: Always prepended. It tells the operator to treat everything its tools return as untrusted data.
activation.promptBodyHint: Edit how the operator introduces itself and how it works.
activation.callerIdentityNote: EDDI substitutes your token when it makes the call. It is never stored in the conversation, and is only ever sent back to this deployment.
activation.rebuildWarning: Saving builds a new operator agent and removes the current one. Your existing operator conversation will not carry over.
activation.environmentHint: Where the operator agent itself runs. It can still read any environment.

none.label: No credentials
none.description: Tool calls carry no Authorization header. Works only when this EDDI deployment has authentication disabled.

caller-identity.label: Your identity
caller-identity.description: Tool calls run as the signed-in user, with that user's permissions and audit trail. Required when authentication is enabled.

approval.verifiedTitle: Resolved from the actual API call config; re-checked immediately before execution — if the request changes before then, execution is refused.
approval.previewOnlyTitle: This call runs additional setup steps before executing, so this is a best-effort preview — the actual request may differ and is not re-checked before execution.
approval.bodyTruncated: Body shown truncated for display — approval still covers the full request.
approval.diffLoading: Loading the stored version to compare against…
approval.diffFailed: Couldn't load the stored version to compare against — the full proposed document is below.
approval.diffForbidden: Comparing against the stored version needs editor access — the full proposed document is below.
approval.diffRedactionNote: Credential values are redacted in the proposed version, so they appear as changes here even when unchanged.

escalation.heading: This request grants further capability
escalation.dynamicAgentCreation: This group may create new agents while it runs. Those agents are not themselves approval-gated.
escalation.dynamicAgentRecruitment: This group may pull other existing agents into its discussions.
escalation.autoApproveOnTimeout: Approvals for this resource are granted automatically when they time out, with nobody watching.
escalation.agentCreatedWithoutGate: This agent is being created with no approval gate. Every write it later makes will execute unsupervised.
escalation.agentCreatedWithBroadEndpoints: This agent is being created with write access to its API — not limited to reads.
escalation.agentCreatedWithExternalTools: This agent is being created with every tool an external MCP server offers. That server decides what those are, and can change them later.
escalation.unchecked: The body was too long to scan for capability grants — read it in full before approving.
escalation.inlineCredential: This request embeds what looks like a credential literal instead of a ${vault:…} reference. A written-in secret is stored in plain text and cannot be rotated from the vault — reject and ask for the vault reference.

approval.blockedSelfTarget: An agent may not modify its own definition, and this request targets the operator's own agent ({{agentId}}). Approving is unavailable for the whole batch while it is present — reject, and make this change from that agent's own page.
approval.blockedGateCarrying: This request writes an LLM configuration that sets its own approval gate (toolApprovals), which would replace the gate reviewing it. Approving is unavailable for the whole batch while it is present — reject, and change the gate from the agent's own page.
approval.blockedGateUnverifiable: This request writes an LLM configuration whose body cannot be read in full — it is either too large to display or not valid JSON — so it cannot be confirmed free of an approval-gate override. Approving is unavailable for the whole batch while it is present — reject, and make this change from the agent's own page.
approval.blockedGateUnpinned: This request writes an LLM configuration but is not pinned, so what actually runs can differ from what is shown here and cannot be confirmed free of an approval-gate override. Approving is unavailable for the whole batch while it is present — reject, and make this change from the agent's own page.
